subject: POC: Mercantile - scope alignment & success plan
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@mercantile.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@mercantile.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC: Mercantile - scope alignment & success plan

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear framing on the three primary workflows you want to validate. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an aligned kickoff plan.

Recap of agreed POC goals (high level)
- Use case A: Customer support routing (classification + suggested replies) — target precision on intent mapping and reply quality.
- Use case B: Product search enhancement (relevance + embedding rerank) — uplift vs current baseline.
- Use case C: Live query streaming for session-aware recommendations (new ask; discussed during call).

Proposed success criteria (draft)
- Support: intent classification F1 >= 0.86 on agreed eval set; suggested reply acceptance rate >= 35% in manual review.
- Search: NDCG@10 uplift >= 12% against current production signals.
- Streaming queries: 95th-percentile end-to-end latency < 350ms for median payloads; graceful degradation fallback to batch rerank when latency SLO breached.

Evaluation plan and timeline (draft)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope + data access lists + sign SOW (attached v1 POC plan).
- Week 1: data ingest + baseline run (Redwood infra; assistance from Mercantile infra).
- Weeks 2–3: focused experiments per use case + daily syncs (Mon/Wed standups).
- Week 4: consolidated evaluation report + handoff session.

Ownership (suggested)
- Redwood: Ben Carter (integration lead), Aditya Rao (solutions/benchmarks), Olga (overall PM/AE).
- Mercantile: Priya (product owner), Jordan (platform lead), security contact for SOC/compliance.

Open items / asks for Mercantile
1) Confirm you want the streaming query use case included in the initial POC — confirm acceptance criteria above or propose adjustments.
2) Provide a sample dataset (anonymized) or S3 access for baseline ingestion + a short list of failing examples you want us to prioritize.
3) Share Mercantile's procurement timeline and any required BOQ/PO language so we can prepare the SOW.
4) Security: if you need SOC2 evidence we can attach a snapshot (v2026-10) and we can schedule a short security review call.

Attachments: Mercantile_POC_v1.xlsx (POC plan & milestones), SOC2_snapshot_2026-10.pdf (evidence snapshot), SOW-draft-mercantile.docx (initial SOW template).

Next step: if you confirm the streaming add and the timeline above, we’ll update the POC plan and propose a kickoff date.

—
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Priya Sharma <priya@mercantile.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@mercantile.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC: Mercantile - scope alignment & success plan

Thanks, Olga — solid write-up. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

1) Confirm streaming query inclusion: yes, we want to include Use case C in the initial POC. Important add: queries may be routed through our authz layer; the model responses must respect tenant-level access controls. Can Redwood validate end-to-end authz behavior in the POC or provide a test harness?

2) Latency SLO: we discussed 350ms in the call. Given our SLA expectations, can we target 95p < 300ms instead? If that forces tradeoffs (e.g., smaller model or more aggressive quantization), please call that out in the revised plan.

3) Success criteria tweaks: for suggested replies can we include an additional qualitative metric — "safety/brand compliance" flag where Mercantile reviewers mark replies as acceptable/needs rewrite. Aim: 90% of accepted replies must be brand-compliant.

4) Compliance: yes, please attach SOC2 snapshot (you included it — thanks). We’ll need to forward to our security team; they may request the runtime architecture diagram and logs retention policy.

5) Timeline: procurement is a bit delayed due to year-end approvals. Can we shift the kickoff by one week (move Week 0 tasks to the week of Nov 30)? We still want a four-week active trial after ingestion.

Attached: procurement_timeline_Mercantile.pdf (internal) — I’ll share with your team separately if needed.

Action for Redwood: please update the POC plan v1 to reflect authz test harness, tightened latency goal (95p < 300ms), and the brand-compliance review step. Also confirm whether the SOC2 snapshot is sufficient or if security will need additional artifacts.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Sharma
Head of Product, Mercantile.ai
priya@mercantile.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: internal - Mercantile scope change impact & owners

Internal note — copying the Mercantile thread here for context. Summary of impact and proposed owner-level changes based on Priya's asks: 

Impact summary
- Streaming authz requirement: adds an integration workstream to validate tenant-level access controls. We’ll need a small-sidecar test harness or an instrumented proxy from Mercantile to validate enforcement.
- Latency tightened to 95p < 300ms: this is achievable but will likely require the following tradeoffs: smaller quantized model + prewarming and aggressive prefix caching OR a regional placement on dedicated capacity (higher cost). Need to scope both options and call out unit economics.
- Brand-compliance review step: add a lightweight human-in-the-loop evaluation (Mercantile reviewers) during Week 3 and add an automated safety classifier threshold for candidate replies.

Proposed owner map (Redwood side)
- Integration & infra: Ben Carter (lead) + one integration engineer (TBD) — responsible for authz harness + ingestion pipeline.
- Benchmarks & evals: Aditya Rao — set up measurement sheets, run NDCG/F1 pipelines.
- Customer success / rollout: Monica Patel — coordinate Mercantile reviewers, daily syncs, and final handoff.
- AE / contract: Olga — SOW/PO movement and approvals.

Action items (internal)
- Ben: draft two options for streaming latency (1) lower-cost quantized path with best-effort 300ms and clear failure modes, (2) dedicated region/Reserved capacity plan with SLA estimate. Due: Fri, Nov 27.
- Aditya: update the eval rubric to include brand-compliance binary flag and a small human-eval rubric. Due: Tue, Nov 30.
- Monica: prepare reviewer invites and a short training doc for brand compliance reviews. Due: Tue, Nov 30.
- Olga: update SOW with a one-week shift and add an explicit "authz testing" scope line. Due: Mon, Nov 29.

Ben

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@mercantile.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@mercantile.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC: Mercantile - scope alignment & success plan

Thanks — that all makes sense and we can accommodate the changes. Quick readout on updates and confirmed next steps: 

1) Scope updates (accepted)
- Streaming queries included. We will build an "authz test harness" pattern that runs alongside your proxy and returns per-request auth decisions so we can validate model outputs only surface permitted tenant data. Ben will follow up with a short technical note and interface spec.

2) Latency tradeoffs (acknowledged)
- We’ll prepare two options in the revised POC plan: 
  Option A (cost-efficient): 95p ~ 300ms using a quantized variant + prewarm/caching. Lower cost but has degraded tail behavior during cold starts.
  Option B (SLA-backed): Reserved capacity in your preferred region with tighter tail guarantees; includes an estimated monthly commit.

3) New evaluation step: brand-compliance reviewer panel. Monica will coordinate (3–5 reviewers) and we’ll add a simple binary label plus short reason field. Aditya will plug this into the evaluation dashboard.

4) Timeline: we accept the one-week procurement shift. Proposed kickoff: week of Nov 30. Active trial window remains 4 weeks post-ingest.

5) Security artifacts: attached SOC2_snapshot_2026-10.pdf here again. Ben will also attach a runtime architecture diagram for your security review by Tue, Nov 30. If Mercantile security needs more, please flag the specific documents (logs retention, KMS flow, HSM integration notes).

Attachments: Mercantile_POC_v2.xlsx (updated plan; includes option A/B), SOC2_snapshot_2026-10.pdf, SOW-draft-mercantile.docx (updated dates).

Next steps / owners (quick)
- Ben: integration options doc + interface spec (due Nov 30).
- Aditya: eval rubric + dashboard updates (due Nov 30).
- Monica: reviewer panel invites + training micro-guide (due Nov 30).
- Olga (me): updated SOW + procurement support; I’ll send the SOW for signature and add our HubSpot deal link.

If that all looks good I’ll send an updated POC plan and a DocuSign SOW link later today.

—
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
